reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures, such as Fig. 1, which shows the 3D models of the Coordinator and the Worker, and Fig. 2, which illustrates the implemented control loop in the proposed VLC-VLS ISAC system. Fig. 3 shows the implemented Sensing and Illumination phases, and Fig. 4 displays an exemplary calibration curve. Fig. 5 depicts the parameters and transmitted commands for a rotation from 0° to 200°, and Fig. 6 presents the measurement results of the comparison between VLS and internal Hall sensor in dark and ambient light conditions.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The system proposed is an Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) system based on Visible Light Communication (VLC) and Visible Light Sensing (VLS). The ISAC system consists of two main parts: the Coordinator and the Worker. The Coordinator uses a Cree MC-E Color RGBW LED to emit light, which is then reflected by a retroreflective foil attached to a rotating cylinder on the Worker. The reflected light is received by the Coordinator, which uses it to determine the rotation angle of the cylinder. The Coordinator then sends commands to the Worker using VLC to adjust the rotation angle. The system uses a PID controller to control the rotation angle and prevent overshoot.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports an average absolute deviation of 1.2° and 1.3° in the rotation angle determination in dark and ambient light conditions, respectively. The maximum absolute error is 5°, which is attributed to imperfections in the retroreflective foil. The results are comparable to those of commercial rotary position sensors, such as the ams AS560, which has a deviation of ±1°.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper demonstrates the feasibility of a VLC-VLS ISAC system for remote sensing and control of a rotating cylinder. The system achieves high accuracy and can adapt to changing ambient light conditions. However, the range of applicable rotation angles is limited due to the necessity of unique reflections from the retroreflective foil. Future work aims to increase the range of rotation angles and improve the accuracy of the rotation angle determination.
